planting.note: Plant divisions or nursery starts in rich, well-drained soil in a sheltered site with light to full shade; growth is very slow, so disturb the thick rootstock as little as possible once sited.

directions: Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light to full shade; this cultivar is one of the best choices for dry, dark corners of the garden where little else thrives. Named for the UK nursery it was sourced from, it carries broad, thick, leathery evergreen leaves marked with distinctive creamy-white vertical streaks, though offsets occasionally show reduced variegation. It is a unique but very slowly-offsetting clone, so choose a permanent position and expect new divisions only after several years. Otherwise treat as a near-maintenance-free evergreen accent for the deepest shade.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, well-drained soil in part sun to light shade; this selection tolerates more light and drought than typical Rohdea once established.

directions: Site in humus-rich, well-drained soil in part sun to light shade, where it tolerates drought once established. Selected from a garden seedling, 'Feelin' Groovy' carries pointed, dark green, deeply grooved evergreen leaves on a clump roughly twice the size of the similar cultivar 'Fukuju Kan'. Unlike many deeply ridged clones, it also produces good clusters of showy dark red fruit, adding winter interest beyond the foliage. Growth is slow and offsetting; divide only occasionally to propagate.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

common_name: Striped Delights Sacred Lily (Striped Seedling Omoto)

planting.note: Plant small divisions in rich, well-drained soil in light shade to full shade; each propagated piece is genetically unique since this cultivar arose as a variegated seedling rather than a stable sport.

directions: Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade to full shade, siting this compact collector's clump where its striped foliage can be admired at close range. 'Striped Delights' arose as an exceptional variegated seedling found in a garden clump of Rohdea japonica 'Taishu', and bears patterned, striped evergreen leaves along with white to cream flowers in spring and summer. Suits rock gardens, fairy gardens, and container plantings; deer and rabbit resistant and tolerant of dry shade once established. Divide sparingly, as the slow-growing rootstock resents disturbance.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, well-drained soil in light shade to full shade; this clone was notoriously difficult to propagate for decades, so handle divisions gently and expect very slow increase.

directions: Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade to full shade. 'Sekkei Nishiki' forms thick, heavily ridged evergreen leaves to about 10 inches long and only an inch wide at the base, each tapering to a sharp point and marked with vertical cream bands and an irregular creamy border. The compact clump stays low and dense, making it well suited to bonsai-style containers, rock gardens, or close-up woodland plantings. Long prized by Japanese collectors but difficult to propagate for decades, it is deer and rabbit resistant and tolerates dry shade once established.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, well-drained soil in light shade to full shade; this woodland collector's clone took decades for growers to source commercially, so treat divisions as precious.

directions: Plant in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade to full shade. 'Miho-no-Matsu' carries sturdy, foot-long evergreen leaves with heavy vertical banding in cream and chartreuse, and mature clumps develop a streaked central ridge pattern in the new spring flush. Winter stalks of showy red fruit add seasonal interest beyond the variegated foliage. Drought-tolerant and deer-resistant once established, it is well suited to dry shade but rewards steady moisture with fuller variegation; divide only occasionally, as growth is slow.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

planting.note: Plant divisions of this dwarf twisted-leaf clone in rich, well-drained soil in light shade to full shade; it is slow-offsetting but notably more vigorous than most twisted-leaf Rohdea selections.

directions: Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade to full shade. 'Shishi' belongs to a highly prized group of dwarf, twisted-leaf Japanese sacred lily cultivars; its narrow, inch-wide dark green leaves curl inward like a ram's horn, giving the plant its name. Expect a slow-offsetting but surprisingly vigorous dwarf clump reaching only about 4 inches tall but spreading to 15 inches wide within five years. A choice specimen for troughs, rock gardens, or close-up shade plantings where its unusual leaf form can be appreciated.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

planting.note: Plant divisions of this dwarf, slowly-offsetting clone in rich, well-drained soil in light shade; best suited to the milder end of its hardiness range.

directions: Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade. Raised from an unnamed seedling resulting from a cross of Rohdea 'Ohyodogawa' and 'Tancho', this cultivar has wavy green leaves that randomly twist, and at 2 inches wide they are notably broader than the similarly dwarf, twisted-leaf cultivar 'Shishi'. A slow-offsetting dwarf clump reaching about 4 inches tall by 15 inches wide, it is grown as a horticultural oddity prized by Rohdea collectors for its unusual leaf habit.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

common_name: Tama Hilfiger Sacred Lily (Ridge-Edged Sport Omoto)

planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, well-drained soil in light shade to full shade; this sport is exceptionally slow to propagate, so expect only occasional offsets.

directions: Site in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade to full shade. 'Tama Hilfiger' arose as a sport of the Japanese cultivar Rohdea 'Tamagawa Ryu'. Wide, dark green leaves carry a narrow creamy-white border running from tip to mid-leaf edge, paired with a creamy-white central ridge, giving the rosette a distinctly dressed-up look. It is exceptionally slow to propagate, so new divisions will be scarce for years after planting; otherwise treat as a near-maintenance-free evergreen collector's accent for deep shade.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

common_name: Wrath of Kan Sacred Lily (Corrugated Streaked Omoto)

planting.note: Plant divisions of this vigorous selection in rich, well-drained soil in light shade; it increases somewhat faster than most thickly corrugated Rohdea cultivars.

directions: Grow in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade. Bred from a seedling of Rohdea japonica 'Setsukan Nishiki', 'Wrath of Kan' bears upright, thickly corrugated evergreen leaves randomly streaked with creamy white. It was selected for combining dramatic, heavily ribbed texture with notably better vigor than most similarly corrugated clones, forming a slowly expanding clump to about 20 inches tall and wide. A striking textural specimen for a collector's shade border.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden

planting.note: Plant divisions in rich, well-drained soil in light shade; variegation develops as the season progresses, so do not judge young plants on spring foliage alone.

directions: Site in humus-rich, well-drained soil in light shade to full shade. 'Yori-Kaku-no-Matsa' emerges solid green in spring, then develops uneven horizontal creamy-white banding that appears in late summer and persists through winter, paired with bright red fruit stalks for seasonal contrast. This compact, evergreen groundcover-type clump suits rock gardens, living walls, and container plantings as a filler. Tolerant of dry shade once established; divide only occasionally, since growth is slow.
sources: Plant Delights Nursery / Juniper Level Botanic Garden
